claim: Humans have 13 class II myosin heavy chain genes.
source: Humans have 13 class II myosin heavy chain genes.
evidence: This is a statement of fact about the number of class II myosin heavy chain genes in humans, presented as established knowledge.

claim: Three class II myosin heavy chain genes encode for the heavy chains of paralogs that are widely expressed in nonmuscle tissue.
source: Most of these encode for the heavy chains of skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle myosins, but three encode for the heavy chains of paralogs that are widely expressed in nonmuscle tissue.
evidence: This statement describes the distribution of myosin heavy chain genes, drawing on established scientific knowledge.

claim: The three nonmuscle myosin paralogs are called NM2-A, NM2-B and NM2-C.
source: These are commonly called NM2-A, NM2-B and NM2-C, each with different heavy chains encoded by the MYH9, MYH10 and MYH14 genes, respectively (Berg et al., 2001; Vicente-Manzanares et al., 2009).
evidence: This nomenclature is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: NM2-A, NM2-B, and NM2-C heavy chains are encoded by the MYH9, MYH10 and MYH14 genes, respectively.
source: These are commonly called NM2-A, NM2-B and NM2-C, each with different heavy chains encoded by the MYH9, MYH10 and MYH14 genes, respectively (Berg et al., 2001; Vicente-Manzanares et al., 2009).
evidence: This genetic information is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Nonmuscle class II myosins are molecular motors involved in cytokinesis, cell migration, adhesion and tissue morphogenesis.
source: Nonmuscle class II myosins (NM2) are molecular motors involved in cytokinesis, cell migration, adhesion and tissue morphogenesis (Heissler and Manstein, 2013; Vicente-Manzanares et al., 2009).
evidence: This functional description is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The coiled-coil tail region of the heavy chain of each nonmuscle myosin homodimerizes.
source: The coiled-coil tail region of the heavy chain of each of these myosins homodimerizes and the neck region associates with an essential light chain (ELC) and a regulatory light chain (RLC), creating a hexameric molecule.
evidence: This structural description is based on established knowledge of myosin structure.

claim: The neck region of nonmuscle myosin associates with an essential light chain (ELC) and a regulatory light chain (RLC), creating a hexameric molecule.
source: The coiled-coil tail region of the heavy chain of each of these myosins homodimerizes and the neck region associates with an essential light chain (ELC) and a regulatory light chain (RLC), creating a hexameric molecule.
evidence: This structural description is based on established knowledge of myosin structure.

claim: Individual nonmuscle myosin molecules self-associate via their tails to form bipolar filaments.
source: These individual myosin molecules further self-associate via their tails to form bipolar filaments that are approximately 300 nm in length and contain, on average, either 30 myosin molecules for NM2-A and NM2-B or 16 myosin molecules for NM2-C (Billington et al., 2013; Niederman and Pollard, 1975).
evidence: This assembly behavior is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Nonmuscle myosin bipolar filaments are approximately 300 nm in length.
source: These individual myosin molecules further self-associate via their tails to form bipolar filaments that are approximately 300 nm in length and contain, on average, either 30 myosin molecules for NM2-A and NM2-B or 16 myosin molecules for NM2-C (Billington et al., 2013; Niederman and Pollard, 1975).
evidence: This structural measurement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: NM2-A and NM2-B filaments contain, on average, 30 myosin molecules.
source: These individual myosin molecules further self-associate via their tails to form bipolar filaments that are approximately 300 nm in length and contain, on average, either 30 myosin molecules for NM2-A and NM2-B or 16 myosin molecules for NM2-C (Billington et al., 2013; Niederman and Pollard, 1975).
evidence: This quantitative measurement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: NM2-C filaments contain, on average, 16 myosin molecules.
source: These individual myosin molecules further self-associate via their tails to form bipolar filaments that are approximately 300 nm in length and contain, on average, either 30 myosin molecules for NM2-A and NM2-B or 16 myosin molecules for NM2-C (Billington et al., 2013; Niederman and Pollard, 1975).
evidence: This quantitative measurement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: NM2-A and NM2-B can co-polymerize to form heterotypic filaments in cells.
source: In addition, it has been demonstrated that NM2-A and NM2-B can co-polymerize to form heterotypic filaments in cells (Beach et al., 2014; Shutova et al., 2014).
evidence: This co-polymerization behavior is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The enzymatic activity and filament assembly of each NM2 paralog are regulated by phosphorylation of the RLC by myosin light chain kinase (MLCK) or other cellular kinases.
source: The enzymatic activity and the filament assembly of each of the NM2 paralogs are regulated by phosphorylation of the RLC by myosin light chain kinase (MLCK), or other cellular kinases (Heissler and Sellers, 2016).
evidence: This regulatory mechanism is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Different skeletal muscle myosins-2 have distinct enzymatic and mechanical properties.
source: It has long been known that the different skeletal muscle myosins-2 have distinct enzymatic and mechanical properties from studies in muscle fibers and of isolated proteins (Bottinelli and Reggiani, 2000).
evidence: This statement about skeletal muscle myosins is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Enzymatic studies on S1 or HMM fragments have revealed differences in the steady state and transient state kinetics of the three NM2 paralogs.
source: Similarly, numerous enzymatic studies conducted on the soluble, single-headed subfragment-one (S1) or double-headed heavy meromyosin (HMM) fragments have revealed differences in the steady state and transient state kinetics of the three NM2 paralogs that suggests there is differentiation of function amongst them (Heissler and Manstein, 2011; Kovács et al., 2003; Rosenfeld et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement about kinetic differences is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The enzymatic activity of all three NM2 paralogs is low compared to other myosin 2 family members.
source: The enzymatic activity of all three NM2 paralogs is low compared to other myosin 2 family members.
evidence: This comparative statement is based on established knowledge from prior studies.

claim: Of the three NM2 paralogs, NM2-A has the highest actin-activated ATPase activity.
source: Nevertheless, of the three NM2 paralogs, NM2-A has the highest actin-activated ATPase activity and translocates actin filaments the fastest (Kim et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2003).
evidence: This comparative statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: NM2-A translocates actin filaments the fastest of the three NM2 paralogs.
source: Nevertheless, of the three NM2 paralogs, NM2-A has the highest actin-activated ATPase activity and translocates actin filaments the fastest (Kim et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2003).
evidence: This comparative statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: NM2-B has a four-fold higher duty ratio than NM2-A.
source: NM2-B has a four-fold higher duty ratio than NM2-A, meaning that it will spend a greater proportion of its ATPase cycle strongly bound to actin filaments (Kovács et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2003).
evidence: This quantitative comparison is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The role of myosin bipolar filaments as force generating structures in cells has been clearly demonstrated.
source: The role of myosin bipolar filaments as force generating structures in cells has been clearly demonstrated (Vicente-Manzanares et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement about myosin function is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Myosin filaments can interact with actin filaments of opposite polarity to create a sarcomeric type contractile unit.
source: Myosin filaments can interact with actin filaments of opposite polarity to create a sarcomeric type contractile unit, similar to those found in striated muscles (Ebrahim et al., 2013).
evidence: This functional description is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Myosin filaments may move processively along actin filaments in cells which could aid in the organization of the actin cytoskeleton.
source: They may also move processively along actin filaments in cells which could aid in the organization of the actin cytoskeleton (Beach et al., 2017; Ebrahim et al., 2013; Fenix et al., 2016; Hu et al., 2017) or may serve as protein scaffolds (Joo et al., 2007; Maddox et al., 2007; Piekny and Glotzer, 2008).
evidence: This potential function is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Myosin filaments may serve as protein scaffolds.
source: They may also move processively along actin filaments in cells which could aid in the organization of the actin cytoskeleton (Beach et al., 2017; Ebrahim et al., 2013; Fenix et al., 2016; Hu et al., 2017) or may serve as protein scaffolds (Joo et al., 2007; Maddox et al., 2007; Piekny and Glotzer, 2008).
evidence: This potential function is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The mechanical properties of individual NM2 filaments are unknown.
source: However, despite their fundamental roles in generating force in cells, the mechanical properties of individual NM2 filaments are unknown.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that the current study addresses.

claim: NM2-B filaments are processive even at low-solution viscosity.
source: We find that NM2-B filaments are processive even at low-solution viscosity and that 5 – 10 myosin motor domains per half filament are required to ensure processivity.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: 5-10 myosin motor domains per half filament are required to ensure processivity of NM2-B filaments.
source: We find that NM2-B filaments are processive even at low-solution viscosity and that 5 – 10 myosin motor domains per half filament are required to ensure processivity.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NM2-A filaments are only processive when the viscosity of the solution is raised to mimic that of the intracellular milieu using methylcellulose.
source: In contrast, NM2-A filaments are only processive when the viscosity of the solution is raised to mimic that of the intracellular millieu using methylcellulose or when NM2-A is co-polymerized with NM2-B.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NM2-A filaments are processive when NM2-A is co-polymerized with NM2-B.
source: In contrast, NM2-A filaments are only processive when the viscosity of the solution is raised to mimic that of the intracellular millieu using methylcellulose or when NM2-A is co-polymerized with NM2-B.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both the kinetic and mechanical properties of NM2-A and NM2-B, in addition to the stoichiometry of NM-2 subunits, can tune filament mechanical output.
source: Our data demonstrate that both the kinetic and mechanical properties of these two myosins, in addition to the stochiometry of NM-2 subunits, can tune filament mechanical output.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Altering NM-2 filament composition is a general cellular strategy for tailoring force production of filaments to specific functions.
source: We propose altering NM-2 filament composition is a general cellular strategy for tailoring force production of filaments to specific functions, such as maintaining tension or remodeling actin.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Individual HaloTag-NM2-B filaments moved processively along fluorescently labeled actin filaments attached to a glass coverslip.
source: We found that individual HaloTag-NM2-B filaments moved processively along fluorescently labeled actin filaments attached to a glass coverslip (Figure 1A and B; Video 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, supported by figures and videos.

claim: NM2-B filaments were slightly longer (~300 nm) than the diffraction limited resolution of the TIRF microscope.
source: The NM2-B filaments were slightly longer (~300 nm) than the diffraction limited resolution of our TIRF microscope and usually appeared as slightly elongated objects whose long and short axes could be readily distinguished.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: In the presence of 1 mM ATP, HaloTag-NM2-B filaments showed robust processive motility with a characteristic run length of 1.95 ± 0.12 μm.
source: In the presence of 1 mM ATP, HaloTag-NM2-B filaments showed robust processive motility with a characteristic run length of 1.95 ± 0.12 μm (mean ± SEM) and a velocity of 43 ± 21 nm∙ s−1 (mean ± SD, n = 1463 filaments) (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data, supported by figures.

claim: In the presence of 1 mM ATP, HaloTag-NM2-B filaments showed a velocity of 43 ± 21 nm∙ s−1.
source: In the presence of 1 mM ATP, HaloTag-NM2-B filaments showed robust processive motility with a characteristic run length of 1.95 ± 0.12 μm (mean ± SEM) and a velocity of 43 ± 21 nm∙ s−1 (mean ± SD, n = 1463 filaments) (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data, supported by figures.

claim: GFP-RLC-NM2-B filaments showed the same level of processivity as HaloTag-NM2-B filaments.
source: GFP-RLC-NM2-B filaments showed the same level of processivity as HaloTag-NM2-B filaments.
evidence: This is a comparative observation from the experimental data.

claim: A single NM2-B filament could move on actin with its long axis perpendicular or parallel to the actin filament.
source: A single NM2-B filament could move on actin with its long axis perpendicular or parallel to the actin filament and could flip back and forth between these two modes while moving (Video 2).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, supported by video.

claim: NM2-B filaments could flip back and forth between perpendicular and parallel orientations while moving on actin.
source: A single NM2-B filament could move on actin with its long axis perpendicular or parallel to the actin filament and could flip back and forth between these two modes while moving (Video 2).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, supported by video.

claim: When NM2-B filaments encountered an intersection of two actin filaments, they often paused before continuing along the original filament or switching to the other.
source: When NM2-B filaments encountered an intersection of two actin filaments, they often paused before continuing along the original filament or switching to the other (Video 3).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, supported by video.

claim: When a NM2-B filament was bound to a surface-tethered actin filament, it could simultaneously propel the sliding of a free actin filament.
source: In support of this, when a NM2-B filament was bound to a surface-tethered actin filament, we observed that it could simultaneously propel the sliding of a free actin filament (Video 4).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, supported by video.

claim: Individual myosin filaments can align vertically to form highly registered stacks in cells.
source: In cells, individual myosin filaments can align vertically to form highly registered stacks (Fenix et al., 2016; Hu et al., 2017; Shutova et al., 2014; Verkhovsky et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement about cellular behavior is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Stacking of filaments was occasionally observed in preparations of pure NM2-B in the electron microscope.
source: Stacking of filaments was also occasionally observed in preparations of pure NM2-B in the electron microscope (Billington et al., 2013).
evidence: This observation is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Multi-filament structures dynamically formed in the in vitro motility assays when one myosin filament encountered another while moving along an actin filament.
source: We found that multi-filament structures dynamically formed in our in vitro motility assays when one myosin filament encountered another while moving along an actin filament (Video 6).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, supported by video.

claim: Myosin filament stacks were dynamic and could lose myosin filament units as they moved along actin.
source: The stacks were dynamic and could lose myosin filaments units as they moved along actin (Video 7).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, supported by video.

claim: The duty ratio of a single NM2-B motor (subfragment-one) is likely to be at least 0.23.
source: The duty ratio of a single NM2-B motor (subfragment-one) is a function of the actin and ADP concentration but is likely to be at least 0.23 (Wang et al., 2003).
evidence: This value is based on citation to prior literature.

claim: In the presence of ATP, NM2-B molecules only interact with actin via one motor at a time.
source: In the presence of ATP, NM2-B molecules only interact with actin via one motor at a time (Nagy et al., 2013), so corrections for intrahead gating as shown by Kovács et al. (2007) do not have to be considered.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Myosin 5a has a duty ratio of 0.9 calculated using the experimentally determined single-head duty ratio of 0.67.
source: The processive single molecule double-headed cargo motor, myosin 5a has a duty ratio of 0.9 calculated using the experimentally determined single-head duty ratio of 0.67 and Equation (1) (De La Cruz et al., 1999).
evidence: This calculation is based on citation to prior literature.

claim: About nine NM2-B motors would need to be physically in a position to bind the actin filament to ensure that at least one of these motors is bound to actin at any given time.
source: Assuming that rf ≥ 0.9 is required to allow for processive movements, Equation (1) predicts that about nine NM2-B motors would need to be physically in a position to bind the actin filament to ensure that at least one of these motors is bound to actin at any given time.
evidence: This is a prediction based on mathematical modeling using established equations.

claim: There are, on average, 30 motors per half filament in NM2-B filaments.
source: Since there are, on average, 30 motors per half filament, it is not surprising that NM2-B filaments move processively as single units.
evidence: This quantitative statement is based on prior knowledge and is used to support an inference.

claim: Tail fragments from various myosins II do not form discrete 300 nm bipolar assemblies, but instead polymerize into large irregular aggregates or paracrystalline arrays.
source: Numerous studies have shown that tail fragments from various myosins II do not form discrete 300 nm bipolar assemblies, but instead polymerize into large irregular aggregates or paracrystalline arrays (Cohen et al., 1970; Franke et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The HaloTag-NM2-B tail fragment polymerized into bipolar filaments with roughly the same length and number of molecules as wild-type NM2-B filaments.
source: This chimeric myosin tail fragment polymerized into bipolar filaments with roughly the same length and number of molecules as wild-type NM2-B filaments (Figure 2A, middle panel).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data, supported by figure.

claim: For all three mixing ratios of NM2-B and tail fragments, co-filaments were observed moving processively along actin filaments.
source: For all three mixing ratios, co-filaments were observed moving processively along actin filaments.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: The average percentage of full-length NM2-B in moving filaments was slightly higher than predicted for random association of the HaloTag-NM2-B tail fragment and the full-length myosin molecule.
source: We found that the average percentage of full-length NM2-B in moving filaments was slightly higher than predicted for random association of the HaloTag-NM2-B tail fragment and the full-length myosin molecule.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data analysis.

claim: The characteristic run length decreased as the number of motor domains decreased from 0.98 ± 0.03 μm, when there were on average 18 motors per half filament, to 0.45 ± 0.04 μm at an average of 9 motors per half filament.
source: The characteristic run length decreased as the number of motor domains decreased from 0.98 ± 0.03 μm, when there were on average 18 motors per half filament, to 0.45 ± 0.04 μm at an average of 9 motors per half filament (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data, supported by figure.

claim: The minimum number of NM2-B motors that are required to maintain processive movement is at least 5.
source: The intercept of this line with the x axis is 4.1 ± 1.3 motors per half filament, suggesting that the minimum number of NM2-B motors that are required to maintain processive movement is at least 5.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from analysis of the experimental data.

claim: The velocity of filament movement has little dependence on motor number in NM2-B co-filaments with tail fragments.
source: In contrast to the strong dependence of the run length on the number of NM2-B motors present in the co-filaments, the velocity of filament movement has little dependence on motor number (Figure 2D,E; and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from analysis of the experimental data, supported by figures.

claim: No processive movements of GFP-RLC-NM2-A filaments were observed under identical experimental conditions to NM2-B.
source: Despite having similar numbers of motors/filament as NM2-B filaments, no processive movements of GFP-RLC-NM2-A filaments were observed under identical experimental conditions (Video 11).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, supported by video.

claim: Even binding events of the NM2-A filaments to the actin filaments were rarely observed.
source: Strikingly, even binding events of the NM2-A filaments to the actin filaments were rarely observed.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: NM2-A monomers bound to a coverslip surface smoothly propelled actin filaments in the gliding assay.
source: This was not due to lack of enzymatic or mechanical activity, since NM2-A monomers bound to a coverslip surface smoothly propelled actin filaments in the gliding assay (Video 12).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, supported by video.

claim: Phalloidin has no effect on the movement of actin filaments by NM2-A.
source: Note, that in contrast to a previous study (Diensthuber et al., 2011), we found no effect of phalloidin on the movement of actin filaments by NM2-A (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data that contradicts a prior study.

claim: The viscosity experienced by myosin filaments in cells is likely to be considerably higher than in the aqueous medium used for the in vitro motility studies.
source: The viscosity experienced by myosin filaments in cells is likely to be considerably higher than in the aqueous medium that was used for the in vitro motility studies (Kalwarczyk et al., 2011)
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: HaloTag-NM2-A filaments showed robust processive movement with an average velocity of 133 ± 75 nm ∙ s−1 at 30°C in the presence of 0.5% methylcellulose.
source: Under these conditions, HaloTag-NM2-A filaments showed robust processive movement with an average velocity of 133 ± 75 nm ∙ s−1 (mean ± SD, n = 143) at 30°C (Figure 3A–C and Video 13).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data, supported by figures and video.

claim: Most NM2-A filaments moved to the end of the actin filaments or became stuck at actin-actin junctions in the presence of methylcellulose.
source: We were unable to measure an average run length since most of the NM2-A filaments moved to the end of the actin filaments or became stuck at actin-actin junctions (note vertical lines on kymographs in Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, supported by figure.

claim: When 0.5% methylcellulose was used with HaloTag-NM2-B filaments, the processivity of the filaments greatly increased to the extent that virtually all NM2-B filaments moved the entire remaining length of the actin filament.
source: When 0.5% methylcellulose was used with HaloTag-NM2-B filaments, the processivity of the filaments greatly increased to the extent that virtually all NM2-B filaments moved the entire remaining length of the actin filament (Video 14 and Figure 3D,E).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, supported by video and figure.

claim: NM2-A and NM2-B molecules co-polymerized randomly in vitro.
source: We also show in the present study that NM2-A and NM2-B molecules co-polymerize randomly in vitro consistent with reports that they readily form heterotypic filaments in cells (Beach et al., 2014; Shutova et al., 2017; Shutova et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data, supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Co-filaments containing as few as six to eight molecules of NM2-B in the presence of a majority of NM2-A molecules continue to move processively, albeit with shorter run lengths than filaments containing higher amounts of NM2-B.
source: Our data show that co-filaments containing as few as six to eight molecules of NM2-B in the presence of a majority of NM2-A molecules continue to move processively, albeit with shorter run lengths than filaments containing higher amounts of NM2-B.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: The velocity of mixed NM2-A/NM2-B filaments is strongly dictated by the slower NM2-B.
source: Interestingly, the velocity is strongly dictated by the slower NM2-B which is consistent with experiments using the sliding actin in vitro motility assay when fast and slow myosins are mixed on the surface (Cuda et al., 1997; Harris et al., 1994).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data, supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A cell can tune the mechanical output of a filament by varying its composite ratio of NM2 paralogs.
source: These results imply that a cell can tune the mechanical output of a filament by varying its composite ratio of NM2 paralogs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The rate of movement of the myosin filaments are governed by the rate of detachment of myosin from actin.
source: These results suggest that the rate of movement of the myosin filaments are governed by the rate of detachment of myosin from actin.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: NM2-B is more adapted to a role of maintaining a high static tension level in cells.
source: These data suggest that NM2-B is more adapted to a role of maintaining a high static tension level in cells, whereas NM2-A is geared to more rapid motile activity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: NM2-A is geared to more rapid motile activity.
source: These data suggest that NM2-B is more adapted to a role of maintaining a high static tension level in cells, whereas NM2-A is geared to more rapid motile activity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Formation of heterotypic NM2 filaments is an effective mechanism to fine tune filament mechanical properties between two modes.
source: Our data further show that formation of heterotypic NM2 filaments is an effective mechanism to fine tune filament mechanical properties between these two modes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The rate of dissociation of ADP from both acto-NM2-A and acto-NM2-B motor domains is affected by intramolecular strain that occurs when the two motors of a myosin molecule are bound to adjacent actin monomers in the presence of ADP.
source: The effect of force on the kinetics of NM2 paralogs has not been measured using optical trapping, but a previous transient kinetic study showed that the rate of dissociation of ADP from both acto-NM2-A and acto-NM2-B motor domains is affected by intramolecular strain that occurs when the two motors of a myosin molecule are bound to adjacent actin monomers in the presence of ADP (Kovács et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: NM2-B is significantly more strain dependent than NM2-A.
source: However, this study revealed that NM2-B is significantly more strain dependent than NM2-A.
evidence: This statement is based on citation to prior literature.

claim: Under strained conditions, NM2-B will have a significantly longer lifetime on actin filaments than NM2-A.
source: Since the dissociation of ADP from acto-NM2 limits the rate of dissociation of NM2 from actin, this suggests that under strained conditions, NM2-B will have a significantly longer lifetime on actin filaments than NM2-A.
evidence: This is an inference based on prior literature and established knowledge.

claim: NM2-B filaments might be better suited for maintaining tension on actin filaments in cells.
source: This implies that NM2-B filaments might be better suited for maintaining tension on actin filaments in cells, whereas NM2-A would be more useful as a cargo motor for rapid but unsustained contractions or in the remodeling of the actin cytoskeleton, given its higher motility rate.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: NM2-A would be more useful as a cargo motor for rapid but unsustained contractions or in the remodeling of the actin cytoskeleton.
source: This implies that NM2-B filaments might be better suited for maintaining tension on actin filaments in cells, whereas NM2-A would be more useful as a cargo motor for rapid but unsustained contractions or in the remodeling of the actin cytoskeleton, given its higher motility rate.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: NM2-A is more prominent in the leading edge of cells where there are active actin dynamics.
source: In this regard, it is interesting that NM2-A is more prominent in the leading edge of cells where there are active actin dynamics, whereas NM2-B is typically more concentrated with stress fibers which are linked through adhesion complexes to generate forces on the substrate and where actin is highly dynamic (Beach et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: NM2-B is typically more concentrated with stress fibers which are linked through adhesion complexes to generate forces on the substrate.
source: In this regard, it is interesting that NM2-A is more prominent in the leading edge of cells where there are active actin dynamics, whereas NM2-B is typically more concentrated with stress fibers which are linked through adhesion complexes to generate forces on the substrate and where actin is highly dynamic (Beach et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The longer attachment lifetimes and greater strain dependence of these attachments would allow NM2-B to maintain force more effectively and efficiently than NM2-A.
source: The longer attachment lifetimes and greater strain dependence of these attachments would allow NM2-B to maintain force more effectively and efficiently than NM2-A.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: The rate of movement of the hybrid myosin filaments on actin were not significantly affected by the number of myosin motors available.
source: We also found that the rate of movement of the hybrid myosin filaments on actin were not significantly affected by the number of myosin motors available.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: Tail fragments that were N-terminally fused with either the Halo-tag or a fluorescent fusion protein form bipolar filaments that are similar to those formed by full-length molecules.
source: It is significant that tail fragments that were N-terminally fused with either the Halo-tag or a fluorescent fusion protein (data not shown) form bipolar filaments that, by negatively stained transmission electron microscopy, are similar to those formed by full-length molecules.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: Myosin tail fragments that are not N-terminally capped by GFP or a HaloTag form much longer and thicker aggregates or paracrystals when polymerized either in vitro or when overexpressed in cells.
source: In contrast, numerous studies have shown that myosin tail fragments that are not N-terminally capped by GFP or a HaloTag form much longer and thicker aggregates or paracrystals when polymerized either in vitro or when overexpressed in cells (Cohen et al., 1970; Franke et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The experimentally determined single molecule duty ratio of NM2-A is 0.05.
source: In view of the experimentally determined single molecule duty ratio of 0.05 for NM2-A, it is not surprising that these filaments failed to move processively in the absence of methycellulose.
evidence: This value is stated as an experimentally determined fact.

claim: More than 50 motors are required at one end of a NM2-A bipolar filament to ensure that at least one motor would be attached to an actin filament.
source: Calculations using Equation (1) show that more than 50 motors are required at one end of a NM2-A bipolar filament to ensure that at least one motor would be attached to an actin filament and ensure continuation of a processive run.
evidence: This is a calculation based on mathematical modeling.

claim: There are only about 30 motors available at the end of a bipolar filament.
source: There are only about 30 motors available at the end of a bipolar filament and not all of these are likely to be in a geometrically favorable position for actin filament interaction at any given moment.
evidence: This is based on prior knowledge about filament structure.

claim: The viscosity experienced by objects the size of NM2 filaments in cells is expected to be between one and two orders of magnitude larger than that in a simple aqueous buffer.
source: The viscosity experienced by objects the size of NM2 filaments in cells is expected to be between one and two orders of magnitude larger than that in a simple aqueous buffer.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about cellular viscosity.

claim: 0.5% methylcellulose increases the viscosity by about 25-fold.
source: Therefore, we mimicked elements of the physiological viscosity by adding 0.5% methylcellulose to increase the viscosity by about 25-fold (Kalwarczyk et al., 2011).
evidence: This viscosity increase is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Methylcellulose may act by increasing solution viscosity, reducing the diffusion rate of the NM2-A filaments sufficiently such that upon an instantaneous dissociation from actin, it would not diffuse away before another myosin motor could attach.
source: Methylcellulose may act in two ways in this assay. By increasing solution viscosity, the diffusion rate of the NM2-A filaments is reduced sufficiently such that upon an instantaneous dissociation from actin, it would not diffuse away before another myosin motor could attach and restore processive movement.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental observations.

claim: Methylcellulose is a crowding agent which may influence the kinetics, and therefore the duty ratio of NM2-A.
source: Methylcellulose is also a crowding agent which may influence the kinetics, and therefore the duty ratio of NM2-A (Highsmith et al., 1996).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Inclusion of methylcellulose in assays of NM2-B filament produced a 'parking' behavior, where filaments were unable to detach upon reaching the end of the actin filament.
source: Interestingly, inclusion of methylcellulose in assays of NM2-B filament produced a 'parking' behavior, where filaments were unable to detach upon reaching the end of the actin filament and where multiple myosin filaments accumulated at actin intersections.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: Multiple myosin filaments accumulated at actin intersections in the presence of methylcellulose.
source: Interestingly, inclusion of methylcellulose in assays of NM2-B filament produced a 'parking' behavior, where filaments were unable to detach upon reaching the end of the actin filament and where multiple myosin filaments accumulated at actin intersections.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: The parking behavior of NM2-B filaments at high viscosity has also been observed for smooth muscle myosin filaments under similar assay conditions.
source: The parking behavior of NM2-B filaments at high viscosity has also been observed for smooth muscle myosin filaments under similar assay conditions (Haldeman et al., 2014).
evidence: This comparison is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The spatial self-sorting behavior of NM2-A and NM2-B filaments has been demonstrated to rely on a gradual enrichment of NM2-B in stress fibers during retrograde flow.
source: The spatial self-sorting behavior of NM2-A and NM2-B filaments has recently been demonstrated to rely on a gradual enrichment of NM2-B in stress fibers during retrograde flow (Beach et al., 2014; Shutova et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: NM2-B rich filaments have an enhanced activity to remain bound to actin and will thus tend to track rearwards with retrograde flow.
source: Our results offer an explanation for how NM2-B can become preferentially enriched towards the cell posterior in polarized cells, since NM2-B rich filaments have an enhanced activity to remain bound to actin and will thus tend to track rearwards with retrograde flow.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data.

claim: NM2-A rich filaments have a greater probability of detaching from actin and will thus undergo relatively high rates of turnover and recycling with respect to actin.
source: Conversely, NM2-A rich filaments have a greater probability of detaching from actin and will thus undergo relatively high rates of turnover and recycling with respect to actin (Shutova et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data, supported by citation.

claim: In the in vitro assay system, each moving myosin filament typically has contact with only one actin filament.
source: Another significant difference in our in vitro assays and the cellular environment is that in our system each moving myosin filament typically has contact with only one actin filament.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental conditions.

claim: A single cluster of motor domains emanating from one end of a bipolar filament could potentially have interactions with about a 100 nm stretch along an actin filament.
source: A single cluster of motor domains emanating from one end of a bipolar filament could potentially have interactions with about a 100 nm stretch along an actin filament (Billington et al., 2013).
evidence: This estimate is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Inside a cell, myosin filaments may interact with a bundle of actin filaments or with multiple individual actin filaments.
source: Inside a cell, myosin filaments may interact with a bundle of actin filaments or with multiple individual actin filaments.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about cellular conditions.

claim: Both of these cases would tend to increase the ability of myosin to processively interact with actin within its cellular environment.
source: Both of these cases would tend to increase the ability of myosin to processively interact with actin within its cellular environment.
evidence: This is an inference about cellular conditions.

claim: Studies using super-resolution light microscopy found that individual myosin filaments align to form vertical stacks.
source: Recently, studies using super-resolution light microscopy found that individual myosin filaments align to form vertical stacks.
evidence: This statement refers to findings from prior studies.

claim: The formation of myosin filament stacks appeared to require both actin and myosin dynamics.
source: The formation of these stacks appeared to require both actin and myosin dynamics (Fenix et al., 2016; Hu et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Merging and splitting of multi-filament structures is an intrinsic property of myosin filaments when they are brought into close proximity with each other.
source: Since dynamically treadmilling actin was not present in our in vitro assays, this suggests that merging and splitting of such structures is an intrinsic property of myosin filaments when they are brought into close proximity with each other.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data.

claim: The attraction holding myosin filament stacks together is likely to be electrostatic.
source: The attraction is likely to be electrostatic since fewer filament stacks are observed by electron microscopy as the ionic strength is raised.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental observations.

claim: To form the folded 'off' state, the two motor domains of a single myosin make an asymmetric interaction in which the loop 2 region of one motor interacts with the converter domain of another.
source: To form the folded 'off' state, the two motor domains of a single myosin make an asymmetric interaction in which the loop 2 region of one motor interacts with the converter domain of another (Jung et al., 2008; Wendt et al., 2001).
evidence: This structural description is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: This interaction appears to be broken upon phosphorylation of the regulatory light chains.
source: This interaction appears to be broken upon phosphorylation of the regulatory light chains.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of myosin regulation.

claim: The fact that the stacks can disassemble suggests that the forces holding them together are not large.
source: The fact that the stacks can disassemble suggests that the forces holding them together are not large.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental observations.

claim: Different nonmuscle myosin paralogs have different patterns of expression during development.
source: Studies in mutant mouse models reveal that different nonmuscle myosin paralogs have different patterns of expression during development (for a review, see (Ma and Adelstein, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: In the early embryo, only NM2-A is expressed in the developing visceral endoderm.
source: For example, in the early embryo, only NM2-A is expressed in the developing visceral endoderm (Conti et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Ablation of NM2-A is lethal at embryonic day 6 since the cells cannot form appropriate adhesion complexes between cells.
source: Ablation of NM2-A is lethal at embryonic day 6 since the cells cannot form appropriate adhesion complexes between cells.
evidence: This statement is based on prior research findings.

claim: The NM2-B/NM2-A switch can rescue the early embryonic lethality, but the mouse experiences other defects later in development.
source: The NM2-B/NM2-A switch can rescue the early embryonic lethality, but the mouse experiences other defects later in development (Wang et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: NM2-A is specifically required for placental blood vessel formation.
source: NM2-A is specifically required for placental blood vessel formation and NM2-B is required for neuronal cell migration during brain development (Ma et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: NM2-B is required for neuronal cell migration during brain development.
source: NM2-A is specifically required for placental blood vessel formation and NM2-B is required for neuronal cell migration during brain development (Ma et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In some cases, the opposite paralog cannot functionally substitute, suggesting that each of these myosins have features that are not redundant for some cellular functions.
source: In these cases, the opposite paralog cannot functionally substitute, suggesting that each of these myosins have features that are not redundant for some cellular functions.
evidence: This is an inference based on prior research findings.

claim: Relating light microscopic observations of myosin filaments in cells to their mechanical output is not trivial.
source: Our results suggest that relating light microscopic observations of myosin filaments in cells to their mechanical output is not trivial.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: It is now possible to image single myosin filaments in cells with super-resolution light microscopy.
source: With the advent of super-resolution light microscopy, it is now possible to image single myosin filaments in cells, but most experimental methods used to date are not sufficient to truly understand the composition of the observed filaments (Beach et al., 2017; Fenix et al., 2016; Hu et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Most experimental methods used to date are not sufficient to truly understand the composition of the observed filaments.
source: With the advent of super-resolution light microscopy, it is now possible to image single myosin filaments in cells, but most experimental methods used to date are not sufficient to truly understand the composition of the observed filaments (Beach et al., 2017; Fenix et al., 2016; Hu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a critical assessment supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A cell has several potential mechanisms to mechanically fine tune or regulate the activity of a given myosin filament.
source: In summary, a cell has several potential mechanisms to mechanically fine tune or regulate the activity of a given myosin filament.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: These mechanisms include forming heteromeric filaments composed of two or more NM2 paralogs with differing mechanical properties.
source: These include forming heteromeric filaments composed of two or more NM2 paralogs (or myosin 18A) with differing mechanical properties and controlling the number of myosin molecules in a filament or the phosphorylation status of the regulatory light chain of the myosins in a filament (Beach et al., 2017; Billington et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a summary of potential mechanisms, supported by citations.

claim: These mechanisms include controlling the number of myosin molecules in a filament.
source: These include forming heteromeric filaments composed of two or more NM2 paralogs (or myosin 18A) with differing mechanical properties and controlling the number of myosin molecules in a filament or the phosphorylation status of the regulatory light chain of the myosins in a filament (Beach et al., 2017; Billington et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a summary of potential mechanisms, supported by citations.

claim: These mechanisms include controlling the phosphorylation status of the regulatory light chain of the myosins in a filament.
source: These include forming heteromeric filaments composed of two or more NM2 paralogs (or myosin 18A) with differing mechanical properties and controlling the number of myosin molecules in a filament or the phosphorylation status of the regulatory light chain of the myosins in a filament (Beach et al., 2017; Billington et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a summary of potential mechanisms, supported by citations.

claim: For a given NM2 filament observed in a cell, there can be a wide range of mechanical properties which cannot be estimated by fluorescence intensity alone.
source: This means that for a given NM2 filament observed in a cell, there can be a wide range of mechanical properties which cannot be estimated by fluorescence intensity alone.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: The behavior of individual NM2 filaments within a cell are highly unlikely to be uniform.
source: It follows that that the behavior of individual NM2 filaments within a cell are highly unlikely to be uniform.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: Increases in myosin filament density following a cellular perturbation or movement do not necessarily imply that the mechanical output will scale proportionally.
source: Thus, increases in myosin filament density following a cellular perturbation or movement do not necessarily imply that the mechanical output will scale proportionally.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: The in vitro single filament motility assay is a sensitive way to provide information on the regulation of filament mechanical output.
source: In this respect, the in vitro single filament motility assay is a sensitive way to provide information on the regulation of filament mechanical output and to inform future cell biological studies.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of the experimental approach.
